title: Hocum
summary: Hocum is a corrected placename for a location on or near Secatogue Neck in West Islip, possibly a chief's name or a hook-shaped feature rather than the name of the whole neck.
address_label: Secatogue Neck / West Islip, Suffolk County, New York
map_geometry_source: Approximate general marker for the West Islip/Secatogue Neck landscape discussed by Tooker; exact feature or residence is not identified.
introduction_content: Hocum appears as a correction to earlier histories of West Islip and Secatogue Neck. The source rejects the claim that the entire neck was called Hocum and says the broader neck was no doubt Secatogue.
history_content: Earlier writers connected Hocum with the West Islip neck later owned by the Willets family. The history narrows that claim, suggesting Hocum could refer to a chief who lived there or to a particular part of the neck rather than to Secatogue territory as a whole.
translation_content:
Two possibilities are given for Hocum. It may be a personal name, or it may describe a hook-shaped place, compared with Narragansett and Delaware words for a hook. No settled translation is given.

Why Place Names Matter

“These names can actually help to preserve a language and restore a culture.”

— Dean Gallagher, Restoration of Indigenous Place Names (2021), Audio transcript
land_loss_content: Hocum preserves a correction to a repeated local-history claim. That distinction keeps the possible name visible without replacing Secatogue as the broader place and community name.
whereintheworld_content: The map placement is an approximate general point in the West Islip/Secatogue Neck landscape, not an exact location for a chief's residence or for a specific hook-shaped feature.
